column1: # cracking-rosetta | data/mdxfind-transcodes.tsv
# TYPE <TAB> entry-id <TAB> hash[:salt]:plaintext
# One line per case where hashpipe's `-c` reader cannot parse the vector as the
# entry stores it, and the type's own serialization has to be supplied. john
# writes RVARY as "$rvary$<hex>" where mdxfind wants the bare hex; EPiServer's
# john form is two 0x-prefixed fields separated by a space; dynamic_1602 wraps
# hash and salt in "$dynamic_1602$...$...$$U<user>" and QAS-VASAUTH ignores the
# user field entirely.
# The WPA lines are a different KIND of transcode and are worth naming as such:
# they are not a reshuffle of one line's fields but a re-serialization of a
# binary struct. john stores a handshake as "$WPAPSK$<essid>#<475 chars>", where
# the tail is john's own base64 (the crypt "./0-9A-Za-z" alphabet, NOT RFC 4648)
# over the hccap_t of src/hccap.h; mdxfind and hashcat want hashcat's
# "WPA*02*<mic>*<mac_ap>*<mac_sta>*<essid hex>*<anonce>*<eapol>*<message_pair>".
# tools/wpapsk-transcode.pl does the decode, per the loop in john's src/wpapsk.h.
# These are hints about SPELLING, never claims. tools/attach-mdxfind-ahead.pl
# still has to see the line come back on stdout from `hashpipe -c` pinned to
# the named type, or nothing is written. A line here and the entry's stored
# vector are ONE piece of evidence written twice; the entry's note says so, so
# that a later reader does not count them as two agreeing vectors.
# A LINE IS RETIRED WHEN THE ENTRY LEARNS TO SAY IT ITSELF. PR #8 restated
# eleven rows in mdxfind's own serialization, which is strictly better than a
# hint here: the spelling becomes a vector like any other, with its own
# reads_in. The hint is then dead, and leaving it in is not harmless --
# validate.pl reads a line's PRESENCE beside tier 'vector' as proof the round
# trip was not byte-exact and demands match: ["hash-transcoded"], which would
# then be a concession nothing conceded. Eleven were retired on 2026-09-16 on
# two measured conditions, both required: verify-vectors no longer declares
# the concession, AND either the entry stores this exact payload or some
# vector of it carries mdxfind in reads_in. The second is what covers
# episerver-sid and rvary, which store UPPER-case hex, and dynamic-1401,
# which stores 40 characters where the hint had 32 -- widening the string
# test on hex case instead would have been loosening a check to silence an
# error.
# Read by tools/attach-mdxfind-ahead.pl --transcode.
KECCAK512
